purpose: Source-linked qualitative evidence for all nineteen core method/system studies. Four configuration-specific comparison cases appear in the manuscript; this is not exhaustive experimental extraction or a new benchmark.

observations.observation: TIS uses recorded rollout probabilities to bound correction in hybrid and quantized rollout settings; comparisons examine stability and downstream learning.
observations.limit: Truncated correction is a biased surrogate; the experiments do not imply equivalence to response-level importance sampling.

observations.observation: Unified FP8 precision flow and coordinated quantization granularity address learner-rollout inconsistency, with accuracy and efficiency evaluated in the reported stack.
observations.limit: Path-specific consistency does not establish bitwise identity across arbitrary engines or formats.

observations.observation: The stack combines W8A8 rollout, attention/KV scaling, synchronization, and adopted TIS/MIS; v2 also explores end-to-end FP8.
observations.limit: Learner precision and component settings vary by experiment; system-level gains do not isolate every component.

observations.observation: Longer-run behavior under TIS motivates ACR; invariant scaling addresses quantized weight-update visibility.
observations.limit: Within-paper setting; not a universal failure horizon.

observations.observation: Rollout-aligned QAT and sequence-level TBPO are evaluated jointly and through component ablations for quantized MoE reasoning RL.
observations.limit: The numerical and objective components act on different objects; QAT emulation is distinct from native low-precision arithmetic.

observations.observation: An adaptive mixture of uncorrected and importance-weighted gradients responds to mismatch diagnostics; the paper studies autoregressive and diffusion models.
observations.limit: The adapted quantity is the estimator mixture, not precision; diffusion likelihood semantics differ from the autoregressive formulation.

observations.observation: Asymmetric weight QAT and rollout residual compensation show complementary gains.
observations.limit: Ablation does not establish universal necessity or superiority of asymmetric QAT.

observations.observation: Advantage-guided probability adjustment regulates discrepancy through update influence; robustness and bidirectional-control ablations examine the reported FP8 regimes.
observations.limit: Regulation around a reference range is not unconditional minimization of discrepancy and does not establish native FP4 transfer.

observations.observation: Shared-objective corrections are compared under quantization stress; separate lag experiments test composition. Top-k reconstruction approximates the conditional score expectation.
observations.limit: Quantization stress curves report training accuracy, not a universal held-out ranking. Conditional centering does not recover the on-policy trajectory distribution.

observations.observation: Signed clipping effects motivate BF16-reference calibration; main GRPO endpoints select the best average checkpoint over 500 steps.
observations.limit: Best checkpoint differs from final checkpoint or time-to-quality.

observations.locator: Sections 3-5; Figure 4; Table 1; Appendix B.1 and B.3-B.4
observations.observation: Synchronous native-W4A4 math RL compares BF16, NVFP4, TIS and full TRIAGE over 600/1700 steps. Local directional diagnostics motivate gating and repair.
observations.limit: No direct SC/TIS+SC or KV4 experiment is reported. Population directional trends do not guarantee token-wise contraction.

observations.observation: Guided fake-quantized learner forward with BF16 backward supports joint FP4 expert W/A and KV rollout. Table 6 directly compares TIS+SC at cap 2.
observations.limit: SC uses its best mean checkpoint through 400 steps; task-wise outcomes differ. The local rounding argument is not a global policy guarantee, and learner execution is not native FP4 training.

observations.observation: Selective protection improves INT4 KV fidelity and learning under the retained TIS recipe.
observations.limit: Colocated quota-based partial collection; generation and optimization alternate.

observations.observation: Under BF16 training and FP8 rollout, P3O avoids the evaluated late collapse on Qwen3-8B-Base; the smaller-model comparison shows little separation.
observations.limit: The evaluated FP8 trajectories are short and the baseline has no separate mismatch correction; this is not a universal long-run stability guarantee.

observations.observation: A smooth regularizer supplies corrective gradients outside the Binary-TV trust region; experiments include FP8 rollout and FP8 end-to-end MoE training.
observations.limit: Low-precision results concern the tested architectures and recipes; bounded update weights do not establish global policy improvement.

observations.observation: FP8-rollout comparisons and component ablations separate sampler-referenced candidate construction from post-synchronization inference-gap-aware acceptance.
observations.limit: The practical acceptance proxy is not an unconditional monotonic-improvement certificate; extra evaluation and rollback can affect cost.

observations.observation: Precision ablations identify rollout activation underflow as a key failure source; sparse residual correction improves the evaluated FP4 RL accuracy.
observations.limit: All FP4 experiments use simulation. Hardware-friendly sparsity and overhead analysis do not establish measured native-FP4 speedup.

observations.observation: The system coordinates checkpoint conversion, learner forward, rollout, and weight export under common quantization rules, with explicit high-precision exceptions.
observations.limit: Recipe-level integration is not isolated evidence for every component; MXFP8/NVFP4 are marked Beta and tested model/hardware coverage is bounded.

observations.observation: On Qwen3-8B-Base, native NVFP4 rollout with simulated-quantization training improves quantized endpoint quality over post-RL RTN and reduces measured step time.
observations.limit: QARL evidence must be separated from the larger QAD study; the training matmuls run in BF16 and this is not native FP4 training.
